plans.hypothesis: If the claim holds, the numeric ages of the Late Cretaceous (Chalk) stages on the chronostratigraphic chart will be at least about 300 million years before present.
plans.pass_criterion: Age of the top of the Chalk-bearing Upper Cretaceous (base of Paleogene) and of the base of the Upper Cretaceous are both >= 300 Ma.
plans.fail_criterion: Either age is < 300 Ma (for example, the Upper Cretaceous spans roughly 100.5-66 Ma). Failing this makes 'far more than 300 million years since the latter part of the Secondary' false.
plans.interpretation: 'Secondary period' corresponds to the Mesozoic; 'latter part' corresponds to Late Cretaceous (Chalk). The test is on elapsed time since then, taken from radiometrically calibrated ages and not from Darwin's erosion-rate extrapolation. Modern reading: the erosion-rate assumption is not tested directly, only its implied elapsed time.

dataset.name: International Chronostratigraphic Chart
dataset.why_it_fits: The chart is downloadable and lists numeric boundary ages in Ma for the Cretaceous series and stages, so the Late Cretaceous start and end ages can be read directly.

plans.hypothesis: If the claim holds, GBIF records of native (non-introduced) amphibians will be essentially absent from truly oceanic islands, meaning those never connected to a continent.

plans.fail_criterion: More than 10% of the listed oceanic islands have at least one native amphibian species supported by a verified native occurrence.
plans.interpretation: 'Batrachians' means Amphibia (Anura, Caudata, plus Gymnophiona if present). 'Oceanic islands' means islands of volcanic or coral origin that were never joined to a continent, so continental fragments such as Seychelles, New Zealand and Madagascar are excluded. GBIF establishmentMeans and island/country fields allow introduced frogs to be separated from native ones.

plans.pass_criterion: In a phylogeny built from breed and wild Columba genomes, all breeds are monophyletic with C. livia (including feral and wild populations), other Columba species lie outside as outgroups, and breed ancestry from non-livia species is <5%.
plans.fail_criterion: One or more breeds are sister to or derived from a separate Columba species (non-livia ancestry >=10%), or breeds form clades not including C. livia.
plans.interpretation: 'Aboriginal stocks' means distinct wild species, and 'geographical sub-species' means C. livia populations. The modern equivalent is a genome-wide tree with outgroup species.

dataset.name: NCBI Genome: Columba livia
dataset.why_it_fits: Provides the rock pigeon reference genome and related Columba assemblies and sequence read archives needed for phylogenetic placement of breeds.

plans.hypothesis: If the claim holds, paleotemperature records from both hemispheres will show their coldest glacial interval at the same time within a short lag.
plans.pass_criterion: In at least 80% of paired northern and southern Last Glacial Maximum records, the timing of the coldest interval differs by <= 3 kyr, and the cross-correlation of northern and southern composites peaks within +/-3 kyr of zero lag.
plans.fail_criterion: Median lag between north and south temperature minima is > 5 kyr, or the cross-correlation peak falls outside +/-5 kyr.
plans.interpretation: 'Simultaneous' is read as coincident within dating uncertainty, about a few thousand years. 'Temperature of the whole world cooler' is measured by ice-core isotope and marine proxy temperatures from both hemispheres.

dataset.name: NOAA NCEI Paleoclimatology Data (ice core and marine temperature records)
dataset.publisher: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information
dataset.why_it_fits: Hosts Greenland and Antarctic ice-core isotope series and marine sediment proxies with age models, giving timing of coldest glacial intervals in both hemispheres.

plans.hypothesis: If the claim holds, oceanic islands will hold far fewer species than continental plots of equal area.
plans.pass_criterion: For at least 20 oceanic islands, the median ratio of recorded species richness to that of equal-area continental plots in the same latitude band is < 0.5 for each of birds and vascular plants, significant at p < 0.01 after controlling for sampling effort.
plans.fail_criterion: Median ratio >= 0.8 or no significant difference.
plans.interpretation: 'Species of all kinds' is tested in taxa with good coverage (vascular plants, birds). Equal area is matched using island area and mainland grid cells of that area. Sampling bias in occurrence data is controlled by rarefaction.

dataset.name: GBIF Occurrence Download / Occurrence API (plants and birds)
dataset.why_it_fits: Fields used: speciesKey, decimalLatitude, decimalLongitude, island, countryCode, year. Species counts are computed per island and per equal-area mainland cell.

plans.hypothesis: If the claim holds, many more European-native plant species are naturalised in La Plata and Australia than southern-hemisphere-native species are naturalised in Europe.
plans.pass_criterion: Ratio of the number of European-native species naturalised in Argentina/Uruguay or Australia to the number of southern-hemisphere-native species naturalised in any European region is >= 10.
plans.fail_criterion: Ratio < 3.
plans.interpretation: 'Naturalised' follows GloNAF status classes. 'Southern forms' means species whose native range lies mainly in the southern hemisphere, which requires native-range information from an external source such as POWO joined to GloNAF. 'Cover the ground' and 'beaten the natives' are not measured; only counts of naturalised species are.

dataset.name: Global Naturalized Alien Flora (GloNAF)
dataset.why_it_fits: Provides lists of naturalised alien plant taxa per region (country, state, island) including Argentina, Uruguay, Australia and European countries, allowing counts of naturalised taxa by region.

plans.hypothesis: If the claim holds, nearly all sizeable oceanic islands will have at least one native bat species, and remote ones will often hold endemic bats.
plans.pass_criterion: At least 80% of oceanic islands >100 km2 have >= 1 native bat species in IUCN ranges, and at least 30% of those more than 1000 km from a continent have >= 1 endemic bat.
plans.fail_criterion: Fewer than 60% of the oceanic islands have a native bat, or fewer than 10% of the remote ones have an endemic bat.
plans.interpretation: 'Ærial mammals' means Chiroptera. 'Almost every island' is read as >= 80% of oceanic islands above a minimum size. The size limit is added to avoid tiny islets for which range maps cannot resolve presence.

dataset.name: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species - Mammals spatial data (Chiroptera)
dataset.why_it_fits: Fields used: Chiroptera range polygons, presence/origin codes and endemic status, overlaid on island polygons.

plans.hypothesis: If the claim holds, mean stature velocity by age will be highest in infancy, fall to a low steady rate in mid-childhood, rise again in the early teens, and approach zero in adulthood.
plans.pass_criterion: From mean measured stature by single year of age, velocity at age 0-1 exceeds that at age 5-8; velocity at the pubertal peak (age 10-15) is at least 20% greater than the minimum between ages 5-9; velocity at age >= 19 is < 1 cm/yr.
plans.fail_criterion: No pubertal rise (peak velocity at age 10-15 is < 5% above the 5-9 minimum), or velocity is not highest in infancy.
plans.interpretation: 'Curve of growth' is taken as the age-specific mean of measured stature, from which velocity is estimated by differencing. Cross-sectional means approximate the longitudinal curve. 'Growing age' means the pubertal spurt.

dataset.name: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) Body Measures (BMX) and Demographics
dataset.publisher: US CDC National Center for Health Statistics
dataset.why_it_fits: Fields used: RIDAGEYR/RIDAGEMN (age), RIAGENDR (sex), BMXHT (standing height) and BMXRECUM (recumbent length for children under 2), with survey weights.

plans.hypothesis: If the claim holds, molecular phylogenies will place Perissodactyla closer to Lagomorpha (Leporidae) than to other ungulates, and Lagomorpha closer to Perissodactyla than to Rodentia.
plans.pass_criterion: The most recent common ancestor of Perissodactyla and Lagomorpha is younger than that of Perissodactyla with Artiodactyla, Hyracoidea and Proboscidea, and younger than that of Lagomorpha with Rodentia.
plans.fail_criterion: Perissodactyla is closer to Artiodactyla (or any other ungulate group) than to Lagomorpha, or Lagomorpha is closer to Rodentia than to Perissodactyla.
plans.interpretation: 'Other Ungulates' is read as Artiodactyla plus Hyracoidea and Proboscidea, and 'closely related' as a more recent common ancestor in a dated or topological tree. The morphological transformation argument is not tested, only the phylogenetic conclusion.

dataset.name: TimeTree: The Timescale of Life
dataset.why_it_fits: Provides pairwise divergence times between taxa (e.g. Equus, Ceratotherium, Oryctolagus, Mus, Bos), enabling comparison of divergence times for the claimed relationships.

plans.hypothesis: If the claim holds, boys' and girls' stature velocity curves will have a similar shape, differing mainly in timing, with girls' adolescent acceleration earlier.
plans.pass_criterion: After shifting the girls' curve in time, its correlation with the boys' velocity curve is >= 0.9; the girls' peak velocity age is 1.0-3.0 years earlier than the boys'; the unshifted correlation is lower than the shifted one.
plans.fail_criterion: The peak ages differ by < 0.5 years or girls are later, or the shifted correlation is < 0.7.
plans.interpretation: 'Amplitude' is the peak velocity and 'phase' is the age of onset and peak. Velocity is estimated by differencing mean measured stature by single year of age and sex, using cross-sectional data.

dataset.name: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) Body Measures (BMX) and Demographics
dataset.publisher: US CDC National Center for Health Statistics
dataset.why_it_fits: Fields used: age, RIAGENDR (sex), BMXHT (measured stature) and survey weights, which give weighted mean stature by age and sex.

plans.hypothesis: If the claim holds, measured hard-shelled eggs will always have a longer axis than breadth (prolate), with none being oblate.
plans.pass_criterion: Among at least 1000 measured eggs from at least 100 species, 100% have length/breadth > 1.0 (within measurement error of 2%) and none are oblate.
plans.fail_criterion: Any species' mean length/breadth is < 0.98, or more than 0.5% of eggs measured are oblate.
plans.interpretation: 'Prolate spheroid, never oblate' is read as length exceeding maximum breadth in a solid of revolution. Nearly spherical eggs (owls) are allowed if the ratio is >= 1.
plans.no_dataset_reason: I could not verify a specific public egg-shape dataset with a confirmed DOI or landing page. A search did not find the Stoddard et al. 2017 data deposit, and I will not name an unverified identifier.

plans.hypothesis: If the claim holds, most species will have germ-cell (haploid) chromosome numbers between 6 and 16, with few species below 6 and fewer above 16.
plans.pass_criterion: At least 70% of species with recorded haploid number n have 6 <= n <= 16, and the fraction with n > 16 is smaller than the fraction with n < 6.
plans.fail_criterion: Fewer than 50% of species fall in 6-16, or the fraction with n > 16 exceeds the fraction with n < 6.
plans.interpretation: 'Chromosomes in the germ-nuclei' means the reduced (haploid, n) number. Species-level counts in the Chromosome Counts Database, which covers plants only, are used, so the result applies to plants. Polyploid species are kept, since they are part of the real distribution.

dataset.name: Chromosome Counts Database (CCDB)
dataset.publisher: Tel Aviv University / Rice et al.
dataset.why_it_fits: Fields used: species name, gametic number (n), sporophytic number (2n) and reference, allowing the distribution of n to be computed.

plans.hypothesis: If the claim holds, body weight in a growing human will scale with stature at an exponent close to 3.
plans.pass_criterion: Slope of ln(weight) on ln(height) across measured individuals aged 2-19 is between 2.5 and 3.5, with the 95% CI inside that interval.
plans.fail_criterion: Slope < 2.3 or > 3.7, or CI excluding the interval 2.5-3.5.
plans.interpretation: 'Tend to vary as the cubes' is read as a log-log allometric exponent near 3 for weight against linear stature. Deviation from changes in body proportion is permitted ('mainly though not wholly'), hence the tolerance of +/-0.5.

dataset.name: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) Body Measures (BMX)
dataset.publisher: US CDC National Center for Health Statistics
dataset.why_it_fits: Fields used: BMXWT (measured weight, kg), BMXHT (measured height, cm), age and sex for regression of log weight on log height.

plans.hypothesis: If the claim holds, in plaice the ratio k = W/L^3 will rise with length to a maximum near 30 cm and then decline slowly.
plans.pass_criterion: Mean k by 1 cm length class has its maximum at a length between 25 and 35 cm, with k at the peak >= 5% above k at both the smallest (<15 cm) and largest (>45 cm) classes.
plans.fail_criterion: k is flat (range < 3%), is monotonic, or peaks outside 20-40 cm.
plans.interpretation: k is the Fulton condition factor, computed as W/L^3 in individual fish (the scaling constant is irrelevant). Plaice means Pleuronectes platessa. Size at maturity, about 30 cm, depends on sex and area, so the peak is compared with the survey's maturity data.

dataset.name: ICES DATRAS (Database of Trawl Surveys) - biological sampling (CA) data
dataset.publisher: International Council for the Exploration of the Sea (ICES)
dataset.why_it_fits: Fields used: Valid_Aphia (plaice), LngtClass, IndWgt (individual weight), Maturity and Sex in the CA exchange data, for computing k by length class.

plans.hypothesis: If the claim holds, sunflower spiral families will intersect at a constant, generally non-right angle, with right-angle intersections rare.
plans.pass_criterion: In at least 30 measured sunflower capitula, fewer than 20% of measured spiral crossings are within 5 degrees of 90 degrees, and the crossing angle is constant within a capitulum (SD < 5 degrees).
plans.fail_criterion: More than 50% of crossings are within 5 degrees of 90 degrees, or the angle varies by more than 15 degrees across the disc.
plans.interpretation: 'Isogonal' means constant crossing angle, and 'orthogonal' means 90 degrees. The test is of measured parastichy crossing angles in the capitulum.
plans.no_dataset_reason: I know of no public dataset, verified by me, that records measured parastichy crossing angles in sunflower capitula. Available data are mostly parastichy counts, which cannot decide the claim.

plans.hypothesis: If the claim holds, a 500-year Arizona ponderosa pine ring-width chronology will show a statistically significant spectral peak at about 150 years.
plans.pass_criterion: Spectral analysis (multitaper) of a >= 500-year Arizona Pinus ponderosa chronology shows a peak at 140-160 years significant at 95% against a red-noise null, and the peak holds in at least 2 independent sites.
plans.fail_criterion: No significant peak at 140-160 years in any chronology, or the dominant peak is outside the 130-170 year window.
plans.interpretation: 'Century-smoothed ring widths' is modelled as a low-pass filtered ring-width index. 'Regular periodicity' is a statistically significant spectral line. A 500-year record shows only about 3 cycles, which limits the power of the test.

dataset.name: International Tree-Ring Data Bank (ITRDB), Arizona Pinus ponderosa chronologies
dataset.publisher: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information
dataset.why_it_fits: Provides downloadable ring-width measurement and chronology files (Tucson .rwl and .crn formats) by species and region.

plans.hypothesis: If the claim holds, the measured surface of a biconcave red blood cell will not have constant mean curvature.
plans.pass_criterion: On measured 3D surface profiles of at least 50 discocytes, the standard deviation of mean curvature across the surface is > 30% of its mean, which rules out a constant-mean-curvature surface.
plans.fail_criterion: Standard deviation of mean curvature <= 10% of its mean in most cells, consistent with a constant-mean-curvature surface.
plans.interpretation: 'Surface of equilibrium under surface tension alone' is read as a constant-mean-curvature surface. The test is purely geometric. The proposed alternative forces (osmotic, fluid-crystal) are not tested, and modern membrane bending-elasticity theory is a reinterpretation outside the claim.
plans.no_dataset_reason: I could not verify a specific public dataset of 3D red-cell surface geometry with a confirmed landing page and DOI, and I will not give an unverified identifier.
